violated_contract: When a client deliberately ends a live session whose server owes work on a normal closure (for example /v4/listen finalizing a desktop conversation only on close code 1000), the client must signal that intent with an explicit normal close code. A bare close() sends an empty close frame the server reads as 1005, so the owed finalization is skipped and the artifact stays invisible (in_progress) even though the session ended as designed.
canonical_prevention: Route every intentional client teardown through one owner that closes an OPEN socket with 1000 (leaving not-yet-open sockets to abort their handshake), and cover it with a behavioral test that drives a stop through the production IPC handler against a fake socket and asserts the close code, plus the not-open case.
